title: East-west Pacific temperature contrast gave no clear added six-month Nino 3.4 forecast value in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether the current Nino 3 minus Nino 4 temperature anomaly improved six-month Nino 3.4 forecasts after the model included current Nino 3.4 and its three-month change. Separate monthly linear models used only targets observed by the issue month. We used a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 record and 540 monthly test targets in 1981-2025. The contrast reduced pooled mean squared error from 0.48524 to 0.47548 degrees C squared, a 2.01% reduction. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -10.04% to +14.04%, where negative values mean higher error. Thus, the test did not resolve an added benefit. Checks with three- and twelve-month leads, 30-year training, and a current-only baseline also had intervals that included zero. An independent Decimal calculation checked all 540 primary forecast pairs. Code, forecasts, aggregate results, figures, source hashes, and a retrieval recipe are supplied. The test uses one reconstructed surface record, linear models, and 45 years. It does not establish equal forecast value, identify a physical cause, or measure operational forecast skill.
